# 00.0 Welcome to HTML Fundamentals

## Your First Step into the Web

Every web page you have ever visited starts the same way — with a simple text file written in HTML. HTML is not a programming language; it is a **markup language**, which means it describes and structures content, much like a blueprint describes the rooms and walls of a house. When you learn HTML, you learn how to give shape to ideas on the web.

![Conceptual illustration comparing a house blueprint to an HTML document: on the left, an architectural blueprint sketch of a small house with labeled rooms (kitchen, bedroom, bathroom) drawn in light blue linework on a gridded background; on the right, a simple HTML code snippet with a browser preview of a web page showing a heading, paragraph, and image — connected by arrows and the label 'structure for the web.' The friendly flat-style image uses warm colors and clear annotations to explain that HTML gives structure to web content just as a blueprint gives structure to a house.](./.learn/assets/welcome-html-blueprint.png)

## Why Start with HTML?

This course is designed for absolute beginners — you do not need any prior experience. By the end, you will be able to read, write, and structure your own web pages with confidence. HTML is the foundation of everything you see online, and mastering it is your first step toward creating for the web.

Let's begin building your first page.
